candidates.topic: The Man Who Survived Two Atomic Bombs
candidates.teaser: One man was at ground zero in Hiroshima — and then somehow ended up in Nagasaki three days later.
candidates.video_title: He Survived Both Atomic Bombs — Twice
candidates.video_description: Tsutomu Yamaguchi is the only officially recognized survivor of both atomic bomb blasts in 1945. He was in Hiroshima for work, survived, returned home to Nagasaki, and was bombed again. He lived to 93.
candidates.script: This man was standing 3 kilometers from the Hiroshima bomb when it detonated — and survived. He bandaged his wounds, boarded a train, and went home. Home was Nagasaki. Three days later, the second bomb dropped. He survived that too. Japan's government officially confirmed it in 2009. Tsutomu Yamaguchi lived to 93, and died of stomach cancer — not radiation. Was he the luckiest man alive, or the unluckiest?

candidates.topic: The Color Blue Didn't Exist in Ancient Languages
candidates.teaser: Ancient Greeks described the sky as something other than blue — because that word simply didn't exist yet.
candidates.video_title: Ancient Humans Couldn't See Blue — Here's Why
candidates.video_description: Ancient languages including Greek, Chinese, Japanese, and Hebrew had no word for the color blue. Researchers believe humans may not have perceived it as distinct until they had a word for it. The last major language to develop a blue word was surprisingly recent.
candidates.script: Homer described the ocean as 'wine-dark' — never blue. Ancient Greek had words for red, black, white, yellow — but not blue. Neither did ancient Chinese, Japanese, or Hebrew. When researchers tested a tribe in Namibia today that still has no blue word, they genuinely couldn't distinguish it from green. The last major civilization to invent the word 'blue' was just 4,500 years ago. So did ancient humans actually see the sky differently — or just never notice it?

candidates.topic: The Placebo Effect Works Even When You Know It's Fake
candidates.teaser: Doctors gave patients a sugar pill, told them exactly what it was — and it still worked.
candidates.video_title: Fake Pills Still Work — Even When You Know
candidates.video_description: Harvard Medical School ran a study where patients with chronic pain were told they were receiving a placebo — no deception at all. A significant portion still reported real improvement. The brain's expectation of healing can trigger genuine biological responses.
candidates.script: Harvard doctors handed patients a bottle labeled 'placebo pills — sugar.' They told them exactly what was inside. No tricks. Then they said: take them twice a day. Three weeks later, patients reported a 30% reduction in chronic pain — measurable, real improvement from a pill they knew was fake. Your brain doesn't need to be fooled. It just needs permission to heal. The question is: if you know it's fake and it still works — is it still fake?

candidates.topic: Antarctica Has a Secret River Beneath the Ice
candidates.teaser: Hidden under two kilometers of Antarctic ice, there's a river longer than the Thames — and it's been flowing for millions of years.
candidates.video_title: A Secret River Is Flowing Under Antarctica
candidates.video_description: Scientists confirmed a subglacial river system under East Antarctica stretching over 460 kilometers. It flows beneath nearly 2 kilometers of ice and influences how glaciers move — potentially affecting global sea level rise in ways we don't yet fully understand.
candidates.script: Under two kilometers of solid Antarctic ice, scientists just confirmed a river longer than the Thames — 460 kilometers, flowing in complete darkness, untouched for millions of years. It's not frozen. It runs liquid, kept warm by geothermal heat from the Earth's core below. And here's what worries researchers: this river is quietly lubricating the base of glaciers, making them slide faster toward the ocean. Nobody knew it existed until 2023. What else is hiding under there?

candidates.topic: The Eerie Silence of the WOW! Signal
candidates.teaser: In 1977, a radio telescope picked up a signal from deep space so perfect it looked like alien contact — and we've never heard it again.
candidates.video_title: The Alien Signal We Only Heard Once — 1977
candidates.video_description: The WOW! Signal was detected on August 15, 1977 by astronomer Jerry Ehman using Ohio State's Big Ear telescope. It lasted 72 seconds, matched all theoretical predictions for an interstellar transmission, and has never been detected again despite decades of searching.
candidates.script: On August 15th, 1977, a radio telescope in Ohio picked up a signal from deep space. It was so remarkable that the astronomer monitoring it circled the printout and wrote one word: Wow! It lasted exactly 72 seconds, matched every characteristic scientists predicted an alien transmission would have, and then — nothing. It has never repeated in 47 years of searching. No natural source has ever explained it. We sent a reply into space in 2012. We're still waiting.
